sections.h2: Where do I go for property tax in Burke County?
sections.html:
Burke County's Tax Office is in the Burke Services Building at 110 North Green Street in Morganton, NC 28655, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 5 pm. The main phone is (828) 764-9430, and the mailing address is PO Box 219, Morganton, NC 28680.

The office is split into three divisions. Real Property appraises and assesses land and buildings and answers questions on values, revaluation and appeals. Personal and Business Property handles listings and forms for taxable equipment, vehicles and business assets. Collections bills and collects tax for the county and for the municipalities and fire districts that the Burke tax office serves, so one bill can cover several taxing units.

Collections questions can also go to collections@burkenc.org. If you are selling a house here, start with Collections, since they certify what is owed on a parcel when a deed is to be recorded.

sections.h2: What is the Burke County property tax rate?
sections.html:
Burke County's county-wide rate has been held at 55.5 cents per $100 of assessed value, and the fiscal year 2026-2027 budget kept it unchanged. The budget, adopted on a 5-0 vote and effective July 1, 2026, totals about $120.7 million.

The county reports that its commissioners have lowered the property tax rate on two separate occasions since 2023. Your actual bill can include more than the county rate, because municipal and fire district levies are billed through the same office. Read the rate lines on your bill to see which units apply to your address.

A rate is only half of the formula. The county's assessed value is the other half, and Burke County has a new set of values in preparation for 2027, covered below.

sections.h2: What is the Burke County 2027 revaluation?
sections.html:
The county is running a property tax revaluation project for 2027, and its commissioners scheduled a public hearing on the proposed Schedule of Values and Present Use Schedule of Values for November 16, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in the Burke Services Building. Both schedules were posted on the county website and at the tax office for public inspection.

State law requires every county to reappraise all real property at least every eighth year as of January 1 of the scheduled year. For a county of 75,000 or more people, an early reappraisal can be required when its sales assessment ratio drifts below .85 or above 1.15. In a revaluation year the board of equalization and review finishes its work by December 1, which gives owners a longer window than in an ordinary year.

Questions about the schedules go to the Burke County Tax Department at (828) 764-9430. After new values mail out, compare your notice with recent sales of similar homes nearby before deciding whether to appeal.

sections.h2: When is Burke County property tax due, and what is the calendar?
sections.html:
Burke County bills are due September 1, and North Carolina lets owners pay at face amount through January 5 before interest begins. The table lays out the yearly sequence using the state's statutes.

Burke County property tax year at a glance
StepRule as stated in lawSource
Listing periodFirst business day of January through January 31G.S. 105-307
Taxes dueSeptember 1 of the fiscal yearG.S. 105-360
Last day at face amountBefore January 6G.S. 105-360
Interest, January 6 to February 12%G.S. 105-360
Interest after February 13/4 of 1% per month or fractionG.S. 105-360
Board of equalization and review first meetsBetween the first Monday in April and the first Monday in MayG.S. 105-322
Appeal to Property Tax CommissionWithin 30 days after the board mails its decisionG.S. 105-290

The county mails listing forms every summer for owners to update, sign and return. Return them before the end of the January listing period to avoid a late listing penalty.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Burke County assessment?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Office to review your value first, then request a hearing before the county board of equalization and review, which is the board of commissioners unless the county creates a special board. The request must reach the board before it adjourns.

  • You can ask in writing or appear in person.
  • If the board mailed notice of its own decision fewer than 15 days before adjourning, you have 15 days after the mailing to ask for a hearing.
  • The board mails its decision within 30 days after adjournment.
  • A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, by written notice that states the grounds, copied to the assessor.

After Hurricane Helene, the county offered a one-year reduced assessment as of January 1, 2025 for homes with unrepaired structural damage, with 30 days from receipt of the notice to file a written appeal. That adjustment was a one-year measure, so confirm with the Tax Office how your parcel is valued going forward.

sections.h2: What deed certification does Burke County require when a house sells?
sections.html:
Burke County uses a Delinquent Tax Certification form, under G.S. 161-31, which lets the commissioners require the register of deeds to refuse a transfer deed unless the county tax collector has certified that no delinquent taxes are owed. The form was last revised on April 22, 2026.

The request asks for the GIS PIN or parcel number, grantor and grantee names, the grantee's mailing address, the physical address, the sale price and the acreage transferred. It also asks about mobile homes, personal property such as vehicles, boats or farm equipment, and whether the parcel is in the Present Use Value program and will stay in it. Tax office staff then complete a grid that runs from the current year back ten years and shows deferred taxes and amounts due.

Send the request to the Tax Administrator's office, PO Box 219, Morganton, or email collections@burkenc.org. Your closing attorney will normally file it, but a seller who knows the account is current can speed things up by asking Collections for a payoff before listing.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists for Burke County homeowners?
sections.html:
North Carolina has three relief programs, and Burke County owners apply through the county assessor on Form AV-9 during the listing period, with the county required to accept applications through June 1. Each owner can receive benefit from only one program.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value of a permanent residence, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled whose prior-year income is within $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4% of income at or below the limit and 5% above it up to $58,200, after five years of owning and living in the home.

The circuit breaker defers the excess tax, and the deferred tax for the preceding three years comes due if the owner transfers the home, dies or moves out. Ask the Burke Tax Office for the current forms and check whether a sale would trigger that balance.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Burke County?
sections.html:
Burke County had 88,655 estimated residents on July 1, 2025, only 1.2% above the 2020 base and below the 90,912 counted in 2010. The county holds 41,669 housing units on 506.24 square miles of land.

For 2020 to 2024, owners occupy 74.5% of homes and the median owner-occupied value is $185,400. Median household income is $58,592, median gross rent is $884, and 14.0% of residents are in poverty. About 23.2% of residents are 65 or older. Burke issued 588 building permits in 2025.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Burke County.

faqs.q: What is the Burke County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is 55.5 cents per $100 of assessed value, held steady in the 2026-2027 budget. Municipal and fire district rates are billed in addition where they apply.

faqs.q: Where is the Burke County tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 110 North Green Street in Morganton, in the Burke Services Building, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 5 pm. Call (828) 764-9430.

faqs.q: When are Burke County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1. Payment before January 6 is at face amount, then 2% interest applies through February 1 and 3/4 of 1% a month after that.

faqs.q: When does Burke County reappraise property?
faqs.a: The county is working on a 2027 revaluation. Commissioners set a public hearing on the proposed Schedule of Values for November 16, 2026, and state law requires reappraisal at least every eighth year.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certification to sell a house in Burke County?
faqs.a: Yes, the county uses a Delinquent Tax Certification form so the tax collector can confirm no delinquent taxes before a deed is accepted for recording. Request it from the Tax Office at collections@burkenc.org or (828) 764-9430.
